1000_day_selling_leads_gmb.txt.video_summary: This video teaches a step-by-step system for setting up a lead generation business using Google My Business (GMB) to acquire leads for local businesses without ads or cold calling, and then monetizing those leads by selling them or contracting the work.
1000_day_selling_leads_gmb.txt.title: How I Make $1000/day Selling Leads to Local Businesses (Using GMB)

sections.title: Introduction to the Lead Generation System
sections.premise: The speaker introduces a lead generation system that brings in hundreds of leads to sell to business owners for thousands of dollars a month, requiring zero ads or cold calling.
sections.conclusion: The speaker shows proof of earning over $3,000 in a single day and generating 674 calls in a week using this fully automated system with zero startup costs.

sections.title: How the GMB System Works
sections.premise: The system works by getting leads through Google My Business (GMB), where business profiles show up for customer searches like "plumber" or "cleaner."
sections.conclusion: The goal is to get the business profile to show up as the number one search result across the whole city, generating leads that can be monetized by selling them directly, contracting the work, or charging a monthly fee for the page.

sections.title: Setting Up Your GMB Profile: City and Niche Selection
sections.premise: The first step to setting up the system is choosing a city and a niche/service, recommending local cities and niches like car detailing, house cleaning, or skilled trades such as plumbing.
sections.conclusion: The speaker recommends using SEMrush and Google Maps to verify demand (at least 400 searches/month) and competition, suggesting to target cities where two of the top three competitors have under 100 reviews.

sections.title: Creating and Verifying Your GMB Profile
sections.premise: After selecting a city and niche, the next step is to come up with a company name using ChatGPT and then set up the GMB profile on business.google.com, choosing "local store" and adding a commercial building address.

sections.conclusion: A fragmented personality across son, CEO, husband roles is not sustainable — the best version of yourself is one integrated version.

sections.conclusion: Bloom's highlight YouTube channel, launched 90 days ago posting 20 longs a day, is already matching the core channel's lead-gen revenue.

sections.title: Tozi Founders and CPG Distribution Strategy
sections.premise: The founders of Tozi blue corn tortilla chips just launched in H-E-B in Texas and want to build a generational business.
sections.conclusion: Suggested next moves are Sprouts and Target for national footprint alongside TikTok Shop and Amazon to serve the other 49 states.

sections.title: Custom Porsche Cayenne Build
sections.premise: He won a 2017 Cayenne Turbo S on Bring a Trailer during a 7-Eleven pitch and shipped it to Eurowise in North Carolina.
sections.conclusion: Older customized cars have more soul than new ones, and this 700hp off-road British Racing Green build becomes the Aspen family car.

sections.title: Austin Town Hall and Daily Routine
sections.premise: The team is gathering for the May 2026 town hall so every employee knows the full company mission across nutrition, pop, and energy lines.
sections.conclusion: Simplicity wins with diet — chicken thighs, white rice, and one red meat meal daily keep his ADHD in check for cognitive performance.

sections.title: Influencer Program Four Pillars
sections.premise: Rather than compete on college campuses feet-on-the-ground, Bloom scales digitally and lets competitors do the category education.
sections.conclusion: The four pillars are paid influencer priced at half your Meta CPM, gifting to micros, TikTok Shop affiliates built in-house, and product placement for reach.

sections.title: Target Pitch and Magnolia-Scale Partnership
sections.premise: After a four-year courtship starting with greens powder and energy drinks, Bloom flew to Minneapolis for a major Target leadership meeting.
sections.conclusion: Target's Magnolia partnership lead joined the meeting to discuss a food/beverage partnership of that scale, with a Valentine's Day 2027 activation planned.

sections.title: TikTok Shop Launch Playbook
sections.premise: Bloom's new Daily Hydration product with 5g collagen and clear whey sold 30,000 boxes in 10 days on TikTok Shop via FBT fulfillment.
sections.conclusion: The key is velocity and volume — seeding top 200 affiliates managed via Discord and having them all post in the same 24-hour window to overwhelm the algorithm and halo Amazon search.

1b_100m_deals_la_show.txt.video_summary: A Bloom founder documents a weekend at Natural Products Expo West, showing how he manages his nutrition and pop portfolios, advises early-stage founders, and treats the expo as relationship-building rather than immediate sales.
1b_100m_deals_la_show.txt.title: 1B 100M Deals La Show

sections.title: Balancing the Bloom Portfolio
sections.premise: Bloom's portfolio spans nutrition, pop, and energy, and while energy performs best, partners in the other portfolios want equal attention.
sections.conclusion: Dedicating the weekend to nutrition and pop is a way to reassure those partners that Bloom is putting equal effort across the whole portfolio.

sections.title: Venice Beach Morning Before the Expo
sections.premise: Before being stuck under fluorescent lights in an expo hall for 13 hours, the team does an outdoor calisthenics grounding workout at Venice Beach.
sections.conclusion: Despite being able to bench 350 pounds, calisthenics like ring dips humble him as they prep for the biggest natural products expo of the year.

sections.title: The Bloom Booth and Nutrition Tap Wall
sections.premise: Bloom brings 30-40 team members and a massive booth featuring pop and nutrition to exhibit to retailers, distributors, and commerce partners like Amazon, TikTok, Walmart, and Target.
sections.conclusion: After three years of trying, the team finally pulls off a tap wall serving fresh greens, clear protein, and creatine on tap.

sections.title: Advising Victor the Young Founder
sections.premise: A young founder named Victor, who funded his brand through dropshipping and TikTok affiliate, questions whether he should be at the expo before his product is ready.
sections.conclusion: The advice is to define a specific customer avatar—like Bloom targeting the Sephora/Ulta girl—and study how successful brands talk to that person before building the brand.

sections.title: Why Expos Matter for Founders
sections.premise: For solo founders walking the floor, the expo's value isn't landing a huge PO that day.
sections.conclusion: It's about combating the loneliness of entrepreneurship and planting seeds with connections that may pay off 18 months later.

sections.title: Danish Founders and the Global Opportunity
sections.premise: Two 25-year-old Danish founders running a multi-million dollar supplement brand ask how Bloom managed cash during rapid growth.
sections.conclusion: Don't worry about profit for the next two years—reinvest everything and don't get greedy, which is how Bloom scaled and how these kids can too.

1b_6_decisions_20s.txt.video_summary: Bloom Nutrition co-founder Greg Levecchia lays out six decisions—leaving comfortable 7/10 situations, refusing to become cautious after failure, building reputation as leverage, skipping networking to build, exploiting youth, and refusing early optimization—that he says determine an entrepreneur's ceiling.
1b_6_decisions_20s.txt.title: 1B 6 Decisions 20S

sections.title: Abandon the 7/10 for the 10/10
sections.premise: The most dangerous place for an entrepreneur is a 7-out-of-10 life that's comfortable enough to prevent change.
sections.conclusion: Greg gave up his multi-million-dollar Mari Fitness PDF business to launch Bloom's pre-workout, then sacrificed each successful product to chase the next bigger moonshot like taking on Monster and Red Bull.

sections.title: Don't Let Failure Make You Skittish
sections.premise: Of the 250 products Greg has launched, over 98% failed, with just five products producing about 85% of revenue.
sections.conclusion: When a major retailer sent back 150,000 cases of the summer SKU on a Wednesday, he started Thursday at zero and went hunting for a new home for the inventory.

sections.title: Reputation Is Your Real Leverage
sections.premise: Starting with no money and not raising capital until Bloom hit $180 million a year, reputation was the only leverage available.
sections.conclusion: Reputation with customers, partners, banks, and credit cards is what unlocks bigger credit lines, more ad spend, and repeat sales—without it, money stops flowing.

sections.title: Skip Networking, Just Build
sections.premise: In your early years you have no utility, so successful people won't network with you—networking is transactional socializing.
sections.conclusion: Only once Bloom hit $150 million a year did the network Greg wanted start coming to him, so the action item is to build something special and let people come.

sections.title: Youth as an Underused Weapon
sections.premise: Greg faced patronizing ageism from 18 to 25 despite showing success, in a culture that dismisses young operators.
sections.conclusion: Get in shape, be groomed, and surround yourself with 21-23 year olds who understand ChatGPT, TikTok Shop and Snapchat—Bloom's team was under 30 for its first five years.

sections.title: Scale the Unscalable, Skip Optimization
sections.premise: Early entrepreneurs worrying about profitability or delegation are over-optimizing at the wrong stage.
sections.conclusion: Greg used a Bluetooth keyboard to DM customers and personally trained $9.99 fitness-guide buyers through 100-pound weight loss journeys to generate transformations, and closes by insisting movement and momentum—not timing, confidence, or clarity—make entrepreneurship.

sections.title: Four Things to Start Selling on TikTok Shop
sections.premise: Joel shares the four things a brand should do on day zero to win on TikTok Shop.
sections.conclusion: Be authentic and take the gloves off with content, budget for creator sampling, set up a Discord to house creators, and launch Shopify, TikTok Shop, and Amazon all at once for the halo effect.

sections.title: TikTok Shop Summit and CEO Meeting
sections.premise: Bloom attends the invite-only TikTok Shop Summit in California to speak on a panel, network with top sellers, and meet the CEO of TikTok Shop flown in from China.
sections.conclusion: Bloom positions itself as a partner to break the mold of beverage e-commerce, since 30% of their beverage business is already e-commerce versus 95% of US beverages being bought in retail.
